Discover the documentary source universe for {ruler_name} in {country_name}, {period_start_year}-{period_end_year}, Chapter {chapter_id}. This is source discovery only. Do not extract evidence claims, judge the ruler, assign scores, or write SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON records.

Search broadly in English and relevant local languages. Use general, event-specific, institution-specific, archive, author, title, book, academic, legal, audit, NGO, international-organization, investigative, specialist, and reputable local-news queries. Include favorable, adverse, mixed, and exculpatory perspectives. Find at least {candidate_document_target} distinct documents when the information environment permits; continue beyond that while new source families or consequential topics appear. Preserve inaccessible books, paywalled papers, blocked pages, and metadata-only records as candidates with the correct access status. Search results are leads, not evidence.

Research lenses:
{layered_lenses}

Chapter guidance:
{compact_guide}

Return a short source-landscape note followed by exactly one physical machine line for every distinct candidate URL. Each line starts SOURCE_CANDIDATE_JSON: and contains JSON fields: url, title, publisher, document_type, access_status, chapter_ids, likely_topics, discovery_query. access_status must be unopened, opened, accepted, rejected, or access_blocked. During this stage use unopened, opened, or access_blocked; accepted and rejected belong to later inspection. chapter_ids must include {chapter_id}. Do not omit a candidate merely because it may later prove repetitive or weak. If the information environment genuinely cannot supply the target after varied searches, emit DISCOVERY_SATURATION_BLOCKER_JSON with discovery_id `{chapter_id}`, a nonempty searches_attempted array, and a concrete limitation.
